sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About the Past ('akamira'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('yakasiyana'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('anoti'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Talking About the Past ('dzakaita'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('zvakasiyana'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('chakamhara'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Shona Cultural & Everyday Context (Lesson 1): This expression ('Mitsvairo yasungirirwa pamiti mirefu kuti anotsvaira, agokwanisa kutsvaira akamira.' — "Mitsvairo yasungirirwa on / at miti mirefu that / so that he/she tsvaira agokwanisa to / at tsvaira he/she (past) mira.") reflects how Shona speakers connect daily family life, work, and community relationships across urban towns and rural homesteads ('kumusha') in Zimbabwe..

Crate Fruit Trading ('Mabhanana, Maorenji, Maapuro') at Wholesale Markets: At bustling wholesale produce markets like Mbare Musika in Harare or Sakubva in Mutare, crates and boxes ('mabhokisi') of bananas from Honde Valley, oranges from Mazowe, and apples from Nyanga are traded daily..

Flag Colours, Design & the National Symbols of Zimbabwe: Adopted at Independence on 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe's national flag ('mureza weZimbabwe') is rich in symbolism: green represents agriculture and the land's flora, yellow stands for mineral wealth (gold, platinum, and diamonds), red commemorates the blood shed for independence, black represents the heritage of the majority population, white symbolizes peace, and the soapstone Zimbabwe Bird ('Hungwe') connects the modern nation to Great Zimbabwe..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — History & Heritage: Why is Great Zimbabwe called 'Masvingo eGreat Zimbabwe'?
options: Because 'masvingo' means tall green trees
Because it is located beside the Indian Ocean
Because 'masvingo' means modern glass buildings
Because 'masvingo' means fortified dry-stone walls or enclosures
review_exercises.correct_answer: Because 'masvingo' means fortified dry-stone walls or enclosures
review_exercises.explanation: 'Masvingo' refers to the monumental stone enclosures built by ancestors of the Shona people.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Wildlife & Nature: In 'zvipembere zviviri zviri kufura uswa', what are the two rhinoceroses doing?
options: Grazing on grass
Drinking water from the river
Sleeping under a shady tree
Running across the mountain

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — National Flag Colours: Which five colours appear on the national flag of Zimbabwe ('mureza weZimbabwe')?
options: Blue, purple, orange, pink, and grey
Green (girinhi), yellow (yero), red (tsvuku), black (tema), and white (chena)
Only green and white
Red, blue, and gold only
review_exercises.correct_answer: Green (girinhi), yellow (yero), red (tsvuku), black (tema), and white (chena)
review_exercises.explanation: The Zimbabwean flag features horizontal stripes of green, yellow, red, and black with a white triangle bearing the Zimbabwe Bird.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Water Storage & Households: Why are Jojo tanks ('matangi emvura eJojo') placed on elevated brick or steel stands?
options: To serve as watchtowers for wildlife
To dry maize and groundnuts in the sun
To store household water and provide gravity pressure for taps
To shelter livestock during the rainy season
review_exercises.correct_answer: To store household water and provide gravity pressure for taps
review_exercises.explanation: Elevated water tanks store borehole or municipal water so households have a reliable supply.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 9 — Translate this new cumulative sentence: 'Nzvimbo iyi inoratidza nhoroondo yakakosha yevanhu vekare nemagariro avo.'
options: This place shows the important history of the ancient people and their way of life.
These mountains have many green trees and clean rivers.
The visitors took photographs of the two rhinoceroses.
We learned many Shona words, proverbs, and grammar rules.
review_exercises.correct_answer: This place shows the important history of the ancient people and their way of life.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Nzvimbo iyi inoratidza' = 'This place shows', 'nhoroondo yakakosha' = 'important history', 'yevanhu vekare nemagariro avo' = 'of the ancient people and their way of life'.
